text:
priya: FYI customer on dedicated eu-west reported intermittent 504s and large tail latency on /v1/generate. They supplied an x-request-id: req-0a4c2b9f. Asking infra to collect k8s and node/GPU logs so we can repro.

customer-ops: seeing ~20% of requests return 504 within a 10m window. Example curl they used: curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate -H \"Authorization: Bearer <redacted>\" -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" -d '{\"input\":\"small prompt\"}' --max-time 30

customer-ops: response headers include: HTTP/1.1 504 Gateway Timeout
x-request-id: req-0a4c2b9f
via: envoy

jordan_oncall: noted. Is this consistently eu-west dedicated pool or mixed?

customer-ops: Dedicated pool eu-west-2, pool id: ded-euw-42. Affects model: redwood-v1-large, seq len ~512. Load ~60 rps at peak for that tenant.

alex_infra: ok I'll grab pod logs and node metrics for that timeframe. Quick ask: can you confirm timezone for the timestamps? They reported incidents around 2026-03-15 14:03 UTC.

priya: yes 2026-03-15T14:00:00Z +- 10m. Also they said one pod restarted during the window.

alex_infra: running commands now:
```
kubectl -n redwood get pods -l pool=ded-euw-42 -o wide
kubectl -n redwood logs -l pool=ded-euw-42 -c inference --since=30m --tail=500
kubectl -n redwood describe pod <pod-name>
journalctl -u kubelet --since "2026-03-15 13:30:00" --until "2026-03-15 14:30:00"
ssh node-eu-42-3 sudo nvidia-smi --query-compute-apps=pid,process_name,used_memory --format=csv
```

alex_infra: pulled pod logs, found repeated 5xx from envoy upstream with backend connect timeout 1.5s then cascade. snippet: 
```
[14:03:21] envoy upstream request error: upstream connect error or disconnect before headers (connection reset)
[14:03:22] model-run queue length=48, concurrent_runs=8
[14:03:23] allocation failed: cuda out of memory when allocating 512MB for tensor
```

jordan_oncall: cuda OOM + upstream connect issues suggests the node was overloaded. Any node-level OOM/kubelet events?

alex_infra: node journal shows kubelet OOM kills around 14:02 for worker container, and dmesg shows GPU driver recovering: 
```
[Mar 15 14:02:33] NVRM: GPU at PCI:0000:65:00: GPU has fallen off the bus.
[Mar 15 14:02:35] nvidia: GPU recovery completed.
```

bundle-bot: priya requested a debug bundle: /bundle create --tenant=tenant-83 --since=2026-03-15T13:50Z --until=2026-03-15T14:20Z --include-nodes --label=ded-euw-42

bundle-bot: created debug bundle: https://debug-bundles.redwood.internal/12345 (expires in 7 days)

priya: thanks. customer can you try a quick repro curl with trace headers so we can correlate: curl -v -H \"Authorization: Bearer <redacted>\" -H \"x-request-id: mytest-123\" -d '{\"input\":\"hello\"}' https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate --max-time 30. Send me the x-request-id and exact timestamp.

customer-ops: ran it at 2026-03-15T14:08:12Z, x-request-id=mytest-123, got 200 this time. Intermittent though.

alex_infra: grabbing GPU metrics across nodes for that window: nvidia-smi sampling shows memory spikes up to 95% on node-eu-42-3 and sm utilization pegged. Looks like a hot node + heavy batch at ~14:02 leading to driver reset and pod restart.

priya: action items: (1) infra to cordon node-eu-42-3 and migrate pods, (2) infra to attach the debug bundle link to ticket and include the pod logs + nvidia-smi CSV, (3) support to ask customer for any custom batching or concurrency changes.

alex_infra: will cordon and drain this node now: kubectl drain node-eu-42-3 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force. I'll also add autoscaling limit to cap concurrent_runs on that pool for a short window.

customer-ops: thanks, please keep us posted.

priya: adding notes to the ticket and tagging eng-runtime for follow-up on safer OOM handling and fallbacks. :thumbsup:

jordan_oncall: marking thread resolved-for-now; reopen if repeats after node drain and autoscale tweak."
